title: Fine eyes she had, clear
html_source: Edmund Burke on beauty: “[The] beauty of the eye consists, first, in its clearness; what colored eye shall please most, depends a good deal on particular fancies; but none are please with an eye whose water (to use that term) is dull and muddy. We are pleased with the eye in this view, on the principle upon which we like diamonds, clear water, glass, and such like transparent substances.”
